content.title: Recommendations for management of patients with HF

recommendations: SGLT2 inhibitors (canagliflozin, dapagliflozin, empagliflozin, ertugliflozin, sotagliflozin) are recommended in patients with T2DM at risk of CV events to reduce hospitalizations for HF, major CV events, end-stage renal dysfunction, and CV death. (Class I)
SGLT2 inhibitors (dapagliflozin, empagliflozin, and sotagliflozin) are recommended in patients with T2DM and HFrEF to reduce hospitalizations for HF and CV death. (Class I)
The DPP-4 inhibitor saxagliptin is not recommended in patients with HF. (Class III)
All patients with HF should be periodically screened for anaemia and iron deficiency with full blood count, serum ferritin concentration, and TSAT. (Class I)

Intravenous iron supplementation with ferric carboxymaltose should be considered in symptomatic HF patients recently hospitalized for HF with LVEF ≤50% and iron deficiency (serum ferritin <100 ng/mL or ferritin 100–299 ng/mL with TSAT <20%) to reduce risk of HF hospitalization. (Class IIa)
Erythropoietin-stimulating agents are not recommended for anaemia in HF in absence of other indications. (Class III)
Cancer patients at increased risk for cardiotoxicity should undergo CV evaluation before anticancer therapy, preferably by a cardiologist with cardio-oncology experience. (Class I)
Treatment with an ACE inhibitor and a beta-blocker (preferably carvedilol) should be considered in cancer patients developing LV systolic dysfunction during anthracycline chemotherapy. (Class IIa)
A baseline CV risk assessment should be considered in all cancer patients scheduled to receive cancer treatment with potential to cause HF. (Class IIa)
Tafamidis is recommended in patients with genetic-testing–proven hATTR-CA and NYHA class I or II symptoms to reduce symptoms, CV hospitalization and mortality. (Class I)
Tafamidis is recommended in patients with wtTTR-CA and NYHA class I or II symptoms to reduce symptoms and CV hospitalization. (Class I)

Associated Conditions: Reduced hospitalizations for HF and cardiovascular death
genes.context: Document lists SGLT2 inhibitors as recommended in patients with T2DM at risk of CV events and in patients with T2DM and HFrEF to reduce HF hospitalizations and CV death.
The guideline states that the DPP-4 inhibitor saxagliptin is not recommended in patients with HF.

Associated Conditions: Cardiac amyloidosis-related heart failure (reducing symptoms, CV hospitalization and mortality)
genes.context: Recommendations state tafamidis is recommended for patients with genetic-testing–proven hATTR-CA and for patients with wtTTR-CA (both NYHA class I–II) to reduce symptoms and cardiovascular hospitalizations/mortality, implying involvement of the TTR gene/protein.
